speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the onset of your right knee swelling and whether it was preceded by any trauma or injury?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the child have a history of prolonged bleeding after minor injuries, such as tooth extractions or circumcision, and does he experience frequent or unusually large bruises? REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Panel (PT, PTT, INR)

speaker: Doctor
text: I notice the PT is normal, but the PTT result is missing from your message. Could you please provide the PTT value? Also, has he experienced any joint pain or stiffness in other areas?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Swelling of the right knee. I also have No recent trauma or injury, Familial history of similar symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal PT suggests the extrinsic pathway is intact, so the missing PTT is crucial to rule out Hemophilia A or B given the family history. REQUEST TEST: PTT, Factor VIII, Factor IX.

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal coagulation studies, hemophilia is unlikely, so I suspect a localized inflammatory or infectious process like juvenile idiopathic arthritis. REQUEST TEST: Knee Ultrasound, CBC, ESR, CRP.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound Knee: Compatible with hemarthrosis of the right knee, no evidence of fracture or dislocation. Complete Blood Count: Hemoglobin 12.2 g/dL, Hematocrit 36%, Leukocyte count 7,300/mm3, Platelet count 200,000/mm³, Reticulocyte count 1.2%.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound confirms hemarthrosis, but standard coagulation tests were normal, which strongly suggests Hemophilia A or B with a mild phenotype or a lab error. To definitively rule out a factor deficiency despite normal screening, I need specific factor activity levels. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII Activity, Factor IX Activity, vWF Antigen, vWF Ristocetin Cofactor.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the ultrasound confirmed hemarthrosis but all standard coagulation factors are normal, I must consider rare coagulopathies like Factor XI deficiency or vascular issues. REQUEST TEST: Factor XI Activity, Von Willebrand Disease Panel, Knee MRI.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the confirmed hemarthrosis with normal standard coagulation and vWF studies, I suspect a rare clotting factor deficiency such as Factor XII or a fibrinogen disorder. REQUEST TEST: Factor XII Activity, Fibrinogen Level, Thrombin Time.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Thrombin time: < 2 seconds deviation from control

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal coagulation factors and thrombin time, I suspect a platelet function disorder or a rare factor like Factor XIII deficiency. REQUEST TEST: Platelet Function Assay, Factor XIII Activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the confirmed hemarthrosis with normal standard coagulation studies, I suspect a deficiency in Factor XIII, which is not detected by routine PT or PTT tests. DIAGNOSIS READY: Factor XIII Deficiency
